rows.question: I am expecting to graduate from Mitb in Dec 2026. I have just accepted a job offer with google how much do I need to save to buy a flat nearby for a flat suitable for mitb graduate?
rows.answer:
I can’t tell you how much you personally need to save. That depends on your flat choice, loan type, grant eligibility, and your own finances, which the official sources here do not cover for your case.

In general, the cash/CPF you need depends first on financing. With a bank loan, the minimum downpayment is 25% of the purchase price, and 5% of that must be in cash; OA savings may be used for the rest. With an HDB loan, the minimum downpayment is 20% and it can be fully paid using OA savings. Bank-loan buyers must have a valid Letter of Offer when they exercise the Option to Purchase; HDB-loan buyers must have a valid HFE letter then and when submitting the resale application. MAS/HDB loan rules such as LTV, tenure and minimum cash payment also apply. [5][6][1]

If you take an HDB loan, you must first use your OA savings for the purchase up to the prevailing limits, though each buyer may retain up to $20,000 in OA. CPF use also depends on the flat’s remaining lease, property type and loan type, and CPF can be used for purchase price, housing loan, stamp and legal fees. [1][2][3][4][7]

You may also need upfront cash for the resale Option Fee (up to $1,000) and total deposit (up to $5,000). [6]

Grants may reduce what you need to fund. Families may apply for CPF Housing Grant, EHG, Step-Up Grant and PHG, depending on eligibility. Singles grants can be credited to eligible applicants’ OA and used to offset the purchase price or reduce the housing loan; for the Singles Grant, the income ceiling is $8,000 if buying alone, or $16,000 if buying with family or other singles. [8][9][10][11]

For price context, I couldn’t find nearby-town resale prices in the sources I have. The only price fact provided is that for MITB, flat type ALL, from 2025-10 to 2026-09, there were 0 resale deals as of 2026-10, because MITB is not one of the HDB towns in the resale data. This means there is no official resale price figure here for “nearby” flats. Please check the linked official pages for the latest rules. 

Can't answer:
- How much I personally need to save: needs the user's personal finances, flat choice, loan details and grant eligibility, which this assistant does not use or does not have
- Recent resale prices for nearby towns around MITB: the provided price facts only cover MITB, flat type ALL, 2025-10 to 2026-09, with 0 deals; no nearby-town price facts were provided

policy_candidates.title: Terms and Conditions - Sale and Purchase of An HDB Resale Flat
policy_candidates.text:
Document: Terms and Conditions - Sale and Purchase of An HDB Resale Flat
Section: Terms and Conditions - Sale and Purchase of An HDB Resale Flat > **APPLICABLE TO THE BUYER**

24.5 Where the buyer obtains a housing loan from HDB, he must insure the flat against the risk of fire with HDB’s appointed insurer for a sum not less than the amount determined by HDB. HDB has the right to recall the housing loan if the buyer does not have a valid fire insurance on the flat for the duration of the housing loan.

**25 USE OF CPF SAVINGS**

The use of CPF savings for the purchase of an HDB flat is subject to the CPF Board’s prevailing policies, rules, regulations, usage limits, terms and conditions, which include but are not limited to the following:

(a) The occupiers listed in the resale application are not allowed to use their CPF savings for the purchase of the flat.

(b) The buyer who is using his CPF savings to purchase the flat will have to refund the entire sum of CPF monies used (including accrued interest) to his CPF account when he sells the flat or withdraws his ownership in the flat subsequently.

**26 HOUSING LOAN FROM FINANCIAL INSTITUTION**

26.1 The buyer may obtain a loan from any financial institution regulated by the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) to provide housing loans. The mortgage financing guidelines for housing loans obtained from financial institutions are subject to the prevailing MAS guidelines/policies/rules/directives on housing loans.

Using CPF savings for a home purchase

policy_candidates.title: CPFB | Home buying guide for members above 55
policy_candidates.text:
Document: CPFB | Home buying guide for members above 55
Section: Looking for your retirement home > Additional information > How much CPF savings can be used

How much CPF savings can be used

CPF savings can be used for the purchase price, housing loan, stamp and legal fees.

If you are aged 55 and above and selling your current flat, the CPF refunds will first be used to top up your Retirement Account up to your Full Retirement Sum. The remaining refunds will be retained in your Ordinary Account.

You can check the amount available for use on your [Home ownership dashboard](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/homeownershipdashboard), including the exact amount that you would need to refund to your CPF account upon the sale of your current flat that can be reused for your next flat.

If you are buying a resale flat, use our [Housing Usage Calculator](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/tools-and-services/calculators/cpf-housing-usage) to estimate the amount of CPF savings you may use based on the flat's remaining lease.
section_path: How much CPF savings can be used

policy_candidates.title: Mode of Financing for a Resale Flat
policy_candidates.text:
Document: Mode of Financing for a Resale Flat
Section: Mode of Financing for a Resale Flat > Use of CPF savings

**Retention of up to $20,000 in CPF OA**

Flat buyers taking a housing loan from HDB have the option of retaining up to $20,000 of the available [CPF savings](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/home-ownership/using-your-cpf-to-buy-a-home/retain-20000-in-your-oa-if-you-are-taking-a-housing-loan) in each buyer's OA. The remaining balance in the CPF OA must be used to pay for the flat purchase, before they can take an HDB housing loan. If you need the CPF refund from the sale of your current property to finance the resale flat purchase, please ensure the amount has already been credited to your CPF OA, before you submit the resale application.

**Conditions for use of CPF savings**

Take note of the following conditions for using your CPF savings:

There is a limit on the total amount of CPF savings that can be used for your flat purchase. Once that limit is reached, you will not be able to withdraw more of your CPF savings and have to pay the balance flat purchase price and/ or monthly mortgage instalments in cash

policy_candidates.text:
Document: CPFB | Home buying guide for members below 55
Section: Looking to sell your current HDB flat and buy another? > Securing your retirement while living in your flat > Make a partial capital repayment

Make a partial capital repayment

If you are taking an HDB loan, you can consider making a partial repayment and paying off your housing loan in advance to reduce your financial commitments. Doing so will help to shorten the repayment period, cutting down on the interest that you would need to pay. This can help to increase your savings and further grow your retirement income.

However, do be mindful if you are taking a bank loan as you may incur early repayment charges. Do check with HDB or your bank for more details.

[Learn more](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/article/how-do-i-make-partial-repayment-or-full-repayment-of-my-housing-loan)

policy_candidates.text:
Document: Help - Resale Procedures
Section: Help - Resale Procedures

3.2 Buyers who intend to take a bank loan must have a valid Letter of Offer from a bank/financial institution when they exercise the Option to Purchase.

3.3 Buyers who are not taking any housing loan have to indicate that they are financing the flat purchase fully with their CPF savings and/or cash when they submit their resale application to HDB.

**4 OPTION TO PURCHASE**

4.1 Sellers and buyers of resale flats must use the HDB prescribed Option to Purchase (effective 1 January 2018) as the form of contract in resale transactions. No party is allowed to enter into any other agreement pertaining to the sale and purchase of the flat, as this would be null and void pursuant to the Housing and Development Act. No amendments may be made to the prescribed form.

4.2 Sellers and buyers (or their salespersons) can download the prescribed Option to Purchase form from the HDB InfoWEB (www.hdb.gov.sg). Each form has a unique Serial Number. Sellers and buyers must state the Serial Number of the Option to Purchase when they submit a resale application to HDB.

4.3 Sellers and buyers must declare to HDB the true resale price of the flat. They shall not enter into any supplementary agreement or other agreements or arrangements that may cause the resale price as declared to be inflated or understated.

4.4 The prescribed Option Fee, Deposit and Option Period are given below:

Option Fee - An amount not exceeding $1,000

Deposit - An amount not exceeding $5,000

(Option Fee + Option Exercise Fee = Deposit)

For HDB housing loan

You must decide how much (up to $20,000) to retain in your OA at the point of purchase. For more details, please visit the [HDB site](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/buying-a-flat/flat-grant-and-loan-eligibility/housing-loan/housing-loan-from-hdb).

policy_candidates.text:
Document: Terms and Conditions - Sale and Purchase of An HDB Resale Flat
Section: Terms and Conditions - Sale and Purchase of An HDB Resale Flat > **APPLICABLE TO THE BUYER**

Where there are two or more buyers, the buyers must indicate in the resale application form whether they wish to hold the flat as Joint-Tenants or Tenants-in-Common.

**24 HOUSING LOAN FROM HDB**

24.1 HDB will only grant a housing loan to the buyer who can meet the eligibility criteria. The buyer must comply with HDB’s prevailing policies, rules, regulations, terms and conditions relating to the application and approval of the HDB housing loan as stated on the HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) letter or any other loan assessment process that HDB may decide, including but not limited to the loan tenure, Loan-To-Value (LTV) limit and all other terms and conditions related to the HDB housing loan, which HDB may impose or vary from time to time.

24.2 The buyer who is eligible for and is intending to obtain a housing loan from HDB must have a valid HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) letter when he is granted an Option to Purchase by the seller. The HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) letter must be valid when the buyer submits the resale application.

24.3 The buyer who takes a housing loan from HDB must first use all his CPF savings in his Ordinary Account for the purchase of the flat up to the prevailing limits depending on the remaining lease of the flat before the loan is disbursed. HDB may allow each buyer to retain up to $20,000 in his CPF Ordinary Account or such other amount as HDB may, at its sole discretion, decide (“retention amount”). Once the buyer has endorsed the financial plan for the flat purchase, no change of the plan will be allowed.

24.5 Where the buyer obtains a housing loan from HDB, he must insure the flat against the risk of fire with HDB’s appointed insurer for a sum not less than the amount determined by HDB. HDB has the right to recall the housing loan if the buyer does not have a valid fire insurance on the flat for the duration of the housing loan.

**25 USE OF CPF SAVINGS**

The use of CPF savings for the purchase of an HDB flat is subject to the CPF Board’s prevailing policies, rules, regulations, usage limits, terms and conditions, which include but are not limited to the following:

(a) The occupiers listed in the resale application are not allowed to use their CPF savings for the purchase of the flat.

(b) The buyer who is using his CPF savings to purchase the flat will have to refund the entire sum of CPF monies used (including accrued interest) to his CPF account when he sells the flat or withdraws his ownership in the flat subsequently.

**26 HOUSING LOAN FROM FINANCIAL INSTITUTION**

26.1 The buyer may obtain a loan from any financial institution regulated by the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) to provide housing loans. The mortgage financing guidelines for housing loans obtained from financial institutions are subject to the prevailing MAS guidelines/policies/rules/directives on housing loans.

The buyer will also, where relevant, be required to comply with the prevailing loan guidelines/policies/rules/directives of other relevant authorities (including but not limited to HDB).

26.3 The buyer must check the prevailing MAS loan guidelines/policies/rules/directives before applying for a loan from any financial institution licensed by MAS to provide housing loans. The buyer may refer to the HDB InfoWEB (www.hdb.gov.sg), the MAS website (www.mas.gov.sg) or the financial institutions for such information.

26.5 If the buyer is engaging a private solicitor to act for him in the resale transaction, the buyer must inform HDB of the name/address of his solicitor.

26.6 The buyer who obtains a housing loan from a financial institution is not allowed to switch to an HDB housing loan even if he is eligible for an HDB housing loan.

supplied_policy_evidence.title: CPFB | Home buying guide for members above 55
supplied_policy_evidence.text:
Document: CPFB | Home buying guide for members above 55
Section: Looking for your retirement home > Additional information > How much CPF savings can be used

How much CPF savings can be used

CPF savings can be used for the purchase price, housing loan, stamp and legal fees.

If you are aged 55 and above and selling your current flat, the CPF refunds will first be used to top up your Retirement Account up to your Full Retirement Sum. The remaining refunds will be retained in your Ordinary Account.

You can check the amount available for use on your [Home ownership dashboard](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/homeownershipdashboard), including the exact amount that you would need to refund to your CPF account upon the sale of your current flat that can be reused for your next flat.

If you are buying a resale flat, use our [Housing Usage Calculator](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/tools-and-services/calculators/cpf-housing-usage) to estimate the amount of CPF savings you may use based on the flat's remaining lease.

supplied_policy_evidence.title: Mode of Financing for a Resale Flat
supplied_policy_evidence.text:
Document: Mode of Financing for a Resale Flat
Section: Mode of Financing for a Resale Flat > Use of CPF savings

**Retention of up to $20,000 in CPF OA**

Flat buyers taking a housing loan from HDB have the option of retaining up to $20,000 of the available [CPF savings](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/home-ownership/using-your-cpf-to-buy-a-home/retain-20000-in-your-oa-if-you-are-taking-a-housing-loan) in each buyer's OA. The remaining balance in the CPF OA must be used to pay for the flat purchase, before they can take an HDB housing loan. If you need the CPF refund from the sale of your current property to finance the resale flat purchase, please ensure the amount has already been credited to your CPF OA, before you submit the resale application.

**Conditions for use of CPF savings**

Take note of the following conditions for using your CPF savings:

There is a limit on the total amount of CPF savings that can be used for your flat purchase. Once that limit is reached, you will not be able to withdraw more of your CPF savings and have to pay the balance flat purchase price and/ or monthly mortgage instalments in cash

No party is allowed to enter into any other agreement pertaining to the sale and purchase of the flat, as this would be null and void pursuant to the Housing and Development Act. **24 HOUSING LOAN FROM HDB**

24.1 HDB will only grant a housing loan to the buyer who can meet the eligibility criteria. The buyer must comply with HDB’s prevailing policies, rules, regulations, terms and conditions relating to the application and approval of the HDB housing loan as stated on the HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) letter or any other loan assessment process that HDB may decide, including but not limited to the loan tenure, Loan-To-Value (LTV) limit and all other terms and conditions related to the HDB housing loan, which HDB may impose or vary from time to time.

24.2 The buyer who is eligible for and is intending to obtain a housing loan from HDB must have a valid HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) letter when he is granted an Option to Purchase by the seller. The HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) letter must be valid when the buyer submits the resale application.

24.3 The buyer who takes a housing loan from HDB must first use all his CPF savings in his Ordinary Account for the purchase of the flat up to the prevailing limits depending on the remaining lease of the flat before the loan is disbursed. HDB may allow each buyer to retain up to $20,000 in his CPF Ordinary Account or such other amount as HDB may, at its sole discretion, decide (“retention amount”). Once the buyer has endorsed the financial plan for the flat purchase, no change of the plan will be allowed.

At this stage, you do not have to sign on the OTP. However, you must pay an Option Fee to the flat sellers. The Option Fee should be a sum between $1 and $1,000, to be mutually agreed between you and the flat sellers.

Once the flat sellers have granted the OTP to you, they cannot grant another OTP to other flat buyers until the OTP granted to you has expired.

policy_candidates.text:
Document: Proximity Housing Grant for Singles Buying Resale Flats
Section: Proximity Housing Grant for Singles Buying Resale Flats

If you are buying a resale flat to live with or near your parents/ child, you may apply for the following Proximity Housing Grant (PHG) (Singles):

$15,000 to live with your parents/ child

$10,000 to live near your parents/ child (within 4km)

You may also receive the following housing grants if you meet the eligibility conditions:

[CPF Housing Grant for Resale Flats (Singles)](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/buying-a-flat/flat-grant-and-loan-eligibility/singles/cpf-housing-grant)

[Enhanced CPF Housing Grant (Singles)](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/buying-a-flat/flat-grant-and-loan-eligibility/singles/enhanced-cpf-housing-grant)

Apply for an [HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) letter](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/buying-a-flat/flat-grant-and-loan-eligibility/application-for-an-hdb-flat-eligibility-hfe-letter) via the [HDB Flat Portal](https://homes.hdb.gov.sg/home/landing) for a holistic understanding of your housing and financing options before you embark on your home buying journey. It will inform you upfront of your eligibility to purchase a new or resale flat, as well as the amount of CPF housing grants and HDB housing loan you are eligible for.
section_path: Proximity Housing Grant for Singles Buying Resale Flats

policy_candidates.text:
Document: CPFB | Home buying guide for members below 55
Section: Looking to sell your current HDB flat and buy another? > Now that you've got a flat in mind, how can you go about financing it? > Mortgage servicing ratio

Mortgage servicing ratio

The mortgage servicing ratio (MSR) refers to the portion of a borrower’s gross monthly income that goes towards repaying property loans, also known as monthly instalments (MI).

The MSR is capped at 30% of a borrower's gross monthly income. To be prudent, we recommend capping the MI amount at 25% of your monthly income. Do note that MSR applies only to housing loans for the purchase of a HDB flat, or an executive condominium*.

E.g., If your combined monthly income is $8,000, the maximum monthly instalment allowed is $2,400(30%).

policy_candidates.title: Central Provident Fund (Approved Housing Schemes) Regulations 1986 - Singapore Statutes Online
policy_candidates.text:
Document: Central Provident Fund (Approved Housing Schemes) Regulations 1986 - Singapore Statutes Online
Section: Section 6 Change in amount of monthly instalment
Provision: 6 — Change in amount of monthly instalment

Change in amount of monthly instalment 6. —(1) Where the amount of monthly instalment which a member is required to pay to a lender under a mortgage loan of a house or flat, or to the Housing and Development Board or a Town Council in respect of improvement contributions for upgrading works or lift upgrading works (as the case may be), is increased or reduced because of a change — ( a ) in the rate of interest on the mortgage loan or in the quantum of the mortgage loan disbursed in relation to the house or flat; or ( b ) in the rate of interest on the improvement contribution or in the quantum of the improvement contribution payable, the Board is entitled to make the necessary adjustment when computing the amount of monthly instalment payable by the member. (2) Where a house or flat is jointly owned by 2 or more persons, the Board will, if none of the joint owners by written notice to the Board indicates otherwise, require the monthly instalment payable — ( a ) by the joint owners under a mortgage loan of the house or flat to be in the same proportion as that before the change in the rate of interest on the mortgage loan or in the quantum of the mortgage loan disbursed; or ( b ) by the joint owners in respect of improvement contributions in relation to the house or flat to be in the same proportion as that before the change in the rate of interest on the improvement contribution or in the quantum of the improvement contribution payable.

rows.question: I am a foreigner and I just move to Singapore planning to buy a flat at least 1 million, what is the process that I need to do?
rows.answer:
If you are only a foreigner who has just moved to Singapore, I couldn’t confirm from the official HDB sources I have that you can buy an HDB resale flat. The sources say the buyer must be a Singapore Citizen or Singapore Permanent Resident, at least 21 years old, and must apply with at least one other Singapore Citizen or Singapore Permanent Resident to form a core family nucleus. A single person buying alone must be a Singapore Citizen aged 35 or above. If any buyer/core family member is an SPR, they must have held SPR status for at least 3 years at the time of the HFE application. [1]

If you do meet those status rules, the process is broadly:
1. Apply for an HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) letter first. HDB uses this to assess your eligibility to buy and financing options. [1][2]
2. Make sure you have financing in place: enough CPF/cash/loan, and either an HFE letter for an HDB loan or a bank’s Letter of Offer. [2][3]
3. Check the Ethnic Integration Policy and SPR quota at the OTP stage, when exercising the OTP, and again when submitting the resale application. [2]
4. Submit the resale application through the HDB Flat Portal using Singpass. [1][3]

Other key restrictions: you can buy only one flat for owner-occupation, must physically and continuously occupy it, and there is a 5-year minimum occupation period with further restrictions on renting out and buying other residential property. [1]

Please check the latest HDB page before acting, as HDB applies prevailing rules. [1]

Can't answer:
- Whether a foreigner who has just moved to Singapore can buy an HDB flat without being a Singapore Citizen or Singapore Permanent Resident: the official sources provided only state eligibility for Singapore Citizens and Singapore Permanent Residents
- A full process for every possible non-citizen category beyond HDB resale-flat SC/SPR rules: the provided sources cover resale-flat eligibility and procedure, not all non-citizen situations

Sources:
[1] Terms and Conditions - Sale and Purchase of An HDB Resale Flat: https://www.hdb.gov.sg/e-resale/resale-purchase-of-an-hdb-resale-flat
[2] Eligibility for Buying a Resale Flat: https://www.hdb.gov.sg/business-partners/estate-agents-and-salespersons/guide-for-estate-agents-buying-a-flat/eligibility
[3] Help - Resale Procedures: https://www.hdb.gov.sg/e-resale/resale-procedures

**21 ELIGIBILITY TO PURCHASE**

21.1 The buyer‘s eligibility to purchase the flat is determined with the issuance and subject to the terms and conditions of the HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) letter or any other eligibility assessment process that HDB may decide from time to time.

21.2 HDB in its discretion reserves the right to determine the eligibility conditions in accordance with the prevailing policies, rules and regulations. This includes any policies relating to the ownership or disposal of any residential property as well as any wait-out period to be complied with as may be determined by HDB. Any decision made by the HDB on the buyer’s eligibility to purchase the flat shall be final and conclusive.

21.3 The buyer is eligible to purchase only one flat which must be owner-occupied by the buyer and his immediate family who are authorised by HDB to stay in the flat. 21.5 The buyer must be a Singapore Citizen or Singapore Permanent Resident who is at least 21 years old at the submission of the HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) letter application. policy_candidates.title: Eligibility for Buying a Resale Flat
policy_candidates.text:
Document: Eligibility for Buying a Resale Flat
Section: Eligibility for Buying a Resale Flat

Get your buyer-clients to apply for an HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) letter for a holistic understanding and assessment of their housing and financing options before they embark on their home buying journey.

The HFE letter will inform buyers upfront of their eligibility to purchase a new or resale flat, as well as amounts of CPF housing grants and HDB housing loan they are eligible for.

Inform and update your buyer-clients about the requirements of the [Ethnic Integration Policy (EIP) and Singapore Permanent Resident (SPR) quotas](https://services2.hdb.gov.sg/webapp/BB29ETHN/BB29STREET). The quota requirements should be checked to ensure compliance at each of the following milestones when:

Sellers grant the Option to Purchase (OTP);

Buyers exercise the OTP; and

Buyers and sellers submit their respective portions of the resale application.

Read on to find out more information on [eligibility schemes available and their specific eligibility conditions](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/buying-a-flat/flat-grant-and-loan-eligibility).

policy_candidates.title: Couples and Families
policy_candidates.text:
Document: Couples and Families
Section: Couples and Families > Core family nucleus

A household’s eligibility for housing subsidies and HDB housing loan is assessed based on the core family nucleus, which is formed by the core member(s). Core members refer to the applicant(s) and occupier(s) in an HFE letter application who enable the household to qualify for a flat purchase under an eligibility scheme. All core members must remain in the flat application, and physically reside in the flat during the [minimum occupation period (MOP)](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/buying-a-flat/bto-sbf-and-open-booking-of-flats/conditions-after-buying-a-new-flat?anchor=mop) after the flat purchase. Their names cannot be removed.

You and your siblings, who are orphans and single, i.e., unmarried, divorced, or widowed persons[@], will form a core family nucleus and may apply for a flat from HDB or buy a resale flat on the open market with the following criteria:

All your siblings are listed in the same application, and they are not applying for/ owning/ renting a flat separately

At least 1 of your deceased parents was a Singapore Citizen (SC) or Singapore Permanent Resident (SPR)

@ Divorced or widowed persons who have child(ren) and can form a family unit will not qualify to buy a flat as orphaned siblings.

policy_candidates.title: Managing the Resale Flat Purchase
policy_candidates.text:
Document: Managing the Resale Flat Purchase
Section: Managing the Resale Flat Purchase > Consider your budget

Plan your finances and work out your budget before you search for a suitable flat.

You may use a combination of cash, savings in your CPF Ordinary Account, and a [housing loan from HDB](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/buying-a-flat/flat-grant-and-loan-eligibility/housing-loan/housing-loan-from-hdb) or a [financial institution (FI)](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/buying-a-flat/flat-grant-and-loan-eligibility/housing-loan/housing-loan-from-financial-institutions) regulated by the Monetary Authority of Singapore to buy a flat.

To plan for your flat purchase, [calculate your housing budget](https://homes.hdb.gov.sg/home/calculator/budget) and compare the information on housing loans offered by HDB and our participating FIs.

Learn more about the [mode of financing](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/buying-a-flat/resale-flats/process-for-buying-a-resale-flat/resale-flat-planning/mode-of-financing) for your flat, where we provide a breakdown of the payments required, and the types of housing loans available and financial tools you can use.

Make sure you set aside some cash savings for renovation and other necessary expenses to settle into your new home.

Couples and Families
policy_candidates.text:
Document: Couples and Families
Section: Couples and Families > Core family nucleus

A household’s eligibility for housing subsidies and HDB housing loan is assessed based on the core family nucleus, which is formed by the core member(s). Core members refer to the applicant(s) and occupier(s) in an HFE letter application who enable the household to qualify for a flat purchase under an eligibility scheme. All core members must remain in the flat application, and physically reside in the flat during the [minimum occupation period (MOP)](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/buying-a-flat/bto-sbf-and-open-booking-of-flats/conditions-after-buying-a-new-flat?anchor=mop) after the flat purchase. Their names cannot be removed.

You and your fiancé/ fiancée or spouse will form a core family nucleus. Together with your parents (at least one of your parents must be an SC or SPR), your household may apply for a 3Gen flat from HDB or buy a resale 3Gen flat.

If you intend to buy other flat types, please refer to:

Fiancé and fiancée

Married couples and/or parent(s) with child(ren)

policy_candidates.text:
Document: Eligibility for Selling a Flat
Section: Eligibility for Selling a Flat > Ethnic Integration Policy (EIP) and Singapore Permanent Resident (SPR) quota > About the SPR quota

The SPR quota ensures that SPR families can better integrate into the local community. Malaysians are excluded from this quota because of their close cultural and historical similarities with Singaporeans. Non-Malaysian SPR households applying to buy an HDB resale flat need to be within the SPR quota for the block (8%) and neighbourhood (5%).

policy_candidates.title: Eligibility for Selling a Flat
policy_candidates.text:
Document: Eligibility for Selling a Flat
Section: Eligibility for Selling a Flat > Ethnic Integration Policy (EIP) and Singapore Permanent Resident (SPR) quota > How the EIP and SPR quota work

The EIP quota applies for the sale of an HDB flat. In addition, SPR households who are not Malaysians must also meet the SPR quota.

You may be eligible to sell a flat if:

After the sale of your flat, the number of households of your ethnic group remains within the block and neighbourhood limits. In addition, for non-Malaysian SPR households, the number of SPR households remains within the SPR quota

You and the flat buyer are of the same ethnic group and household citizenship

Flat owners who face genuine difficulties selling their flats at a reasonable price when the EIP quotas have been reached may [write to us](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/write-to-us) for assistance. We will review each case carefully and offer assistance where possible, taking into account the individual circumstances. Read more about [buyback assistance](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/hdb-pulse/news/2022/more-support-for-flat-owners-constrained-by-the-ethnic-inegration-policy).

Section: Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD) > Rates and computation

Example: A Foreigner purchases a unit at a market value of $2 million on 1 Aug 2023 and the ABSD rate of 60% applies.

ABSD rates prior to 16 Dec 2021

All entities will be subject to the new ABSD rate of 65%. Housing Developers are subject to the ABSD rate of 35% and an additional non-remittable ABSD rate of 5% upon stamping, i.e. aggregate ABSD rate of 40%. Such developers may apply for remission on the ABSD rate
of 35% under the [ABSD remission for development of 4 or less units of housing accommodation](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/stamp-duty/for-property/appeals-refunds-reliefs-and-remissions/common-stamp-duty-remissions-and-reliefs-for-property/sites-for-development-of-four-or-less-units-of-housing-accommodation) or [ABSD remission for development of 5 or more units of housing accommodation](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/stamp-duty/for-property/appeals-refunds-reliefs-and-remissions/common-stamp-duty-remissions-and-reliefs-for-property/sites-for-development-of-five-or-more-residential-units).

Entities who are acquiring residential properties with no intention to carry out housing development (i.e. construction and sale of housing units) with respect to the subject property acquired should pay the ABSD rate of 65%.

rows.question: How much would the down payment be for a resale flat in Yew Tee?
rows.answer:
I can’t tell you your exact down payment from the official sources I have, because it depends on how you finance the resale flat. If you use an HDB housing loan, the minimum down payment is 20% of the purchase price, and it can be fully paid using CPF Ordinary Account savings [1]. If you use a bank loan, the minimum down payment is 25% of the purchase price, and at least 5% of the purchase price must be paid in cash [1][2].

For a resale flat, you also need to pay the seller an OTP deposit of $2 to $5,000 during the granting and exercising of the Option to Purchase [2]. HDB’s resale procedures also state the Option Fee cannot exceed $1,000 and the total deposit cannot exceed $5,000 [3].

As price context only: for Choa Chu Kang resale flats (which includes Yew Tee), across all flat types, from 2025-10 to 2026-09, the median resale price was $590,000, based on 1,010 deals [price facts].

If you want, I can help explain which parts are usually cash, CPF, or loan based on your financing method. Please check the latest official page as rules may change.

Can't answer:
- Exact down payment amount for a resale flat in Yew Tee: depends on the buyer's financing arrangement, loan amount and purchase price; the sources only give general minimum down payment rules
- Any personalised affordability or whether the user should buy: needs the user's personal finances, which this assistant does not use

Sources:
[1] CPFB | Home buying guide for members below 55: https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/home-ownership/home-buying-guide-for-members-below-55

policy_candidates.title: CPFB | How much CPF savings you can use for your home purchase
policy_candidates.text:
Document: CPFB | How much CPF savings you can use for your home purchase
Section: How much CPF savings you can use for your home purchase

How much CPF savings you can use for your home purchase

Learn more about the amount of CPF OA savings you can use to purchase a home.

*4 Aug 2025*

*SOURCE: CPF Board*

There is a limit on how much of your CPF Ordinary Account (OA) savings can be used for a home purchase. This is so that you would have enough for your retirement.

This limit differs based on the valuation of the flat at time of purchase, purchase price, type of property, loan type, and age of property.

If the remaining lease of the flat can last the youngest owner until age 95, the amount of CPF savings you can use is capped at the lower of the purchase price and the valuation price at the time of purchase.

Your CPF savings can be used for purchasing a home, but did you know that there are limits in place?

Read on to learn more about using your CPF savings for a home purchase.
section_path: How much CPF savings you can use for your home purchase

policy_candidates.text:
Document: CPFB | How much CPF savings you can use for your home purchase
Section: How much CPF savings you can use for your home purchase > Pointers to keep in mind before purchasing a home

Pointers to keep in mind before purchasing a home

Knowing the maximum amount of CPF savings that you can use for your home would help in budgeting for your home.

This ensures that you would have enough cash on hand for other purposes such as renovation and home appliances.

Keep the following pointers in mind before purchasing a home:

· Choose your loan type wisely. There are more constraints in using your CPF savings for a bank loan as compared to an HDB loan.

· Plan your finances accordingly. Use the [CPF housing usage calculator](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/tools-and-services/calculators/cpf-housing-usage) to calculate the exact amount of CPF that can be used for the flat before purchasing.

· Keep the remaining lease in mind. Properties with shorter remaining leases may have additional CPF usage restrictions.

The [Home Purchase Planner](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/home-ownership/about-home-purchase-planner) lets you explore your home purchase budget, loan options, and how your housing decisions can impact your retirement payout goals.

policy_candidates.text:
Document: CPFB | Home buying guide for members above 55
Section: Looking for your retirement home > Additional information > How much CPF savings can be used

How much CPF savings can be used

CPF savings can be used for the purchase price, housing loan, stamp and legal fees.

If you are aged 55 and above and selling your current flat, the CPF refunds will first be used to top up your Retirement Account up to your Full Retirement Sum. The remaining refunds will be retained in your Ordinary Account.

You can check the amount available for use on your [Home ownership dashboard](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/homeownershipdashboard), including the exact amount that you would need to refund to your CPF account upon the sale of your current flat that can be reused for your next flat.

If you are buying a resale flat, use our [Housing Usage Calculator](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/tools-and-services/calculators/cpf-housing-usage) to estimate the amount of CPF savings you may use based on the flat's remaining lease.
section_path: How much CPF savings can be used

policy_candidates.title: CPF Housing Grant for Singles Buying Resale Flats
policy_candidates.text:
Document: CPF Housing Grant for Singles Buying Resale Flats
Section: CPF Housing Grant for Singles Buying Resale Flats

If you are a first-timer Singapore Citizen (SC) and buying a resale flat on your own, you may qualify for a Singles Grant of $40,000 for the purchase of a 2- to 4- room resale flat or $25,000 for a 5-room resale flat.

If you are buying with your parents or your non-resident spouse or other first-timer single(s) (up to 2 Singles Grant applicants), you may be eligible for a Singles Grant of $40,000 for the purchase of a 2- to 4-room resale flat (i.e. a total of $80,000 for 2 singles) or $25,000 for a 5-room or bigger resale flat (i.e. a total of $50,000 for 2 singles).

In addition, you may also receive the following housing grants if you meet the respective eligibility conditions:

[Enhanced CPF Housing Grant (Singles)](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/buying-a-flat/flat-grant-and-loan-eligibility/singles/enhanced-cpf-housing-grant)

[Proximity Housing Grant (Singles)](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/buying-a-flat/flat-grant-and-loan-eligibility/singles/proximity-housing-grant)

Section: Looking to sell your current HDB flat and buy another? > Securing your retirement while living in your flat > Make a partial capital repayment

Make a partial capital repayment

If you are taking an HDB loan, you can consider making a partial repayment and paying off your housing loan in advance to reduce your financial commitments. Doing so will help to shorten the repayment period, cutting down on the interest that you would need to pay. This can help to increase your savings and further grow your retirement income.

However, do be mindful if you are taking a bank loan as you may incur early repayment charges. Do check with HDB or your bank for more details.

[Learn more](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/article/how-do-i-make-partial-repayment-or-full-repayment-of-my-housing-loan)

policy_candidates.text:
Document: Help - Resale Procedures
Section: Help - Resale Procedures

3.2 Buyers who intend to take a bank loan must have a valid Letter of Offer from a bank/financial institution when they exercise the Option to Purchase.

3.3 Buyers who are not taking any housing loan have to indicate that they are financing the flat purchase fully with their CPF savings and/or cash when they submit their resale application to HDB.

**4 OPTION TO PURCHASE**

4.1 Sellers and buyers of resale flats must use the HDB prescribed Option to Purchase (effective 1 January 2018) as the form of contract in resale transactions. No party is allowed to enter into any other agreement pertaining to the sale and purchase of the flat, as this would be null and void pursuant to the Housing and Development Act. No amendments may be made to the prescribed form.

4.2 Sellers and buyers (or their salespersons) can download the prescribed Option to Purchase form from the HDB InfoWEB (www.hdb.gov.sg). Each form has a unique Serial Number. Sellers and buyers must state the Serial Number of the Option to Purchase when they submit a resale application to HDB.

4.3 Sellers and buyers must declare to HDB the true resale price of the flat. They shall not enter into any supplementary agreement or other agreements or arrangements that may cause the resale price as declared to be inflated or understated.

4.4 The prescribed Option Fee, Deposit and Option Period are given below:

Option Fee - An amount not exceeding $1,000

Deposit - An amount not exceeding $5,000

(Option Fee + Option Exercise Fee = Deposit)

policy_candidates.title: Terms and Conditions - Sale and Purchase of An HDB Resale Flat
policy_candidates.text:
Document: Terms and Conditions - Sale and Purchase of An HDB Resale Flat
Section: Terms and Conditions - Sale and Purchase of An HDB Resale Flat > **APPLICABLE TO THE BUYER**

Where there are two or more buyers, the buyers must indicate in the resale application form whether they wish to hold the flat as Joint-Tenants or Tenants-in-Common.

**24 HOUSING LOAN FROM HDB**

24.1 HDB will only grant a housing loan to the buyer who can meet the eligibility criteria. The buyer must comply with HDB’s prevailing policies, rules, regulations, terms and conditions relating to the application and approval of the HDB housing loan as stated on the HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) letter or any other loan assessment process that HDB may decide, including but not limited to the loan tenure, Loan-To-Value (LTV) limit and all other terms and conditions related to the HDB housing loan, which HDB may impose or vary from time to time.

24.2 The buyer who is eligible for and is intending to obtain a housing loan from HDB must have a valid HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) letter when he is granted an Option to Purchase by the seller. The HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) letter must be valid when the buyer submits the resale application.

24.3 The buyer who takes a housing loan from HDB must first use all his CPF savings in his Ordinary Account for the purchase of the flat up to the prevailing limits depending on the remaining lease of the flat before the loan is disbursed. HDB may allow each buyer to retain up to $20,000 in his CPF Ordinary Account or such other amount as HDB may, at its sole discretion, decide (“retention amount”). Once the buyer has endorsed the financial plan for the flat purchase, no change of the plan will be allowed.

rows.question: My brother transferred his HDB flat to me without selling it, but I need to pay for his CPF refund. Can I take an HDB loan? Can I still use the HDB grant given in HFE?
rows.answer:
I could not confirm from the official sources I have that you personally “need to pay” your brother’s CPF refund in every transfer case. What the rules say is: when a flat is transferred other than by sale, the outgoing owner may be required to refund CPF monies to his own CPF account, and the incoming owner may apply to use the incoming owner’s CPF to pay all or part of that refund, subject to CPF Board approval and conditions.[1] If a share is transferred, CPF principal used plus accrued interest must be refunded based on the member’s share, and extra cash may be needed if that member used more CPF than his share.[2]

On the HDB loan: if you need financing to buy or take over ownership of a flat, you may apply for an HDB housing loan or a loan from a financial institution.[4] HDB will grant a housing loan only if you meet its eligibility conditions, and you must also meet HDB’s credit assessment criteria.[4][5] If you do not meet HDB’s eligibility conditions, you must take a loan from a financial institution if you need mortgage financing.[4] A valid HFE letter is required for an HDB housing loan application for a resale flat, and it must still be valid when the resale application is submitted.[4][5]

On the grant shown in your HFE: I couldn't find this in the official sources I have. The passages say an HFE letter states your eligibility to buy a new or resale flat and the amount of grants and HDB loan you are eligible for, but they do not say whether a grant indicated in HFE can be used for a flat transfer instead of a purchase.[4] Please check the latest official HDB guidance for transfer cases.

Can't answer:
- Whether the HDB grant indicated in the HFE letter can still be used for a flat transfer instead of a purchase: the provided official sources do not cover grant use for transfer cases
- Whether the user personally must pay the brother's CPF refund in this specific case: the sources give general transfer rules only and do not determine the user's exact case outcome

Sources:
[1] Central Provident Fund (Approved Housing Schemes) Regulations 1986 - Singapore Statutes Online: https://sso.agc.gov.sg/SL/CPFA1953-RG12
[2] CPFB | Home buying guide for members below 55: https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/home-ownership/home-buying-guide-for-members-below-55
[4] Housing Loan from HDB: https://www.hdb.gov.sg/buying-a-flat/flat-grant-and-loan-eligibility/housing-loan/housing-loan-from-hdb
[5] Terms and Conditions - Sale and Purchase of An HDB Resale Flat: https://www.hdb.gov.sg/e-resale/resale-purchase-of-an-hdb-resale-flat

policy_candidates.text:
Document: Central Provident Fund (Approved Housing Schemes) Regulations 1986 - Singapore Statutes Online
Section: Section 3A Withdrawal for payment upon transfer (other than by way of sale) of house or flat
Provision: 3A — Withdrawal for payment upon transfer (other than by way of sale) of house or flat

Withdrawal for payment upon transfer (other than by way of sale) of house or flat 3A. —(1) Where a member (called in this paragraph the transferor), being the owner or co‑owner of a house or flat, will or is required to transfer (other than by way of sale) his or her estate or interest in the house or flat to another member (called in this paragraph the transferee), the transferee may apply to the Board to withdraw the whole or any part of the amount standing to the transferee’s credit in the Fund for the payment of any amount which the transferor is required, under these Regulations, to pay to the transferor’s account in the Fund upon the transfer. (2) The Board may approve an application under paragraph (1) subject to such terms and conditions as it may deem fit to impose from time to time.

policy_candidates.title: Terms and Conditions - Sale and Purchase of An HDB Resale Flat
policy_candidates.text:
Document: Terms and Conditions - Sale and Purchase of An HDB Resale Flat
Section: Terms and Conditions - Sale and Purchase of An HDB Resale Flat > **APPLICABLE TO THE SELLER**

34.2 For the purpose of the e-payment and where the seller has appointed HDB to act as his solicitor in the sale of the flat, the seller shall provide his bank account to receive the cash proceeds when submitting the resale application. Unless otherwise specified by HDB, the type of bank account to be provided will depend on the ownership, manner of holding and circumstances for the sale of the flat as follows:

(a) The bank account must be from the 3 local banks, namely, DBS/POSB, OCBC and UOB.

(b) If the flat is solely owned, the bank account must belong to the sole owner.

(c) If the flat is jointly owned and held in joint tenancy, the bank account must be held jointly by all the owners of the flat.

(d) If the flat is jointly owned and held in tenancy-in-common, each individual owner of the flat must provide a bank account belonging to each of them.

(e) If the flat is sold by an executor or administrator of the late flat owner’s estate, the bank account must belong to the estate of the late owner.

(f) If the flat is sold pursuant to a Court Order following a divorce, each individual owner of the flat must provide a bank account belonging to each of them.

(g) If the flat is sold by an Attorney acting under a Power of Attorney or a Donee acting under a Lasting Power of Attorney given by a flat owner, or by a Deputy appointed by the court, the bank account must belong to the payee stated in the Power of Attorney or Lasting Power of Attorney or Court Order, where applicable.

policy_candidates.title: IRAS | Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD)
policy_candidates.text:
Document: IRAS | Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD)
Section: Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD) > Residential properties held on trust - ABSD (Trust)

Any conveyance, assignment or transfer on sale of residential property to a trustee to hold on trust and any instrument chargeable in like manner will be subject to the ABSD (Trust) rate of 65%.

For the purposes of stamp duty, the date of document of the purchase instrument will be taken as the date on which the document is **signed** (i.e. the Acceptance to Option to Purchase/Sale and Purchase Agreement should be signed on the date it is to be executed and delivered to the Vendor). The trust instrument should also be signed, sealed and delivered on the day it is to be executed.

Remission of ABSD (Trust) may be provided via a refund where the conveyance, assignment or transfer on sale of residential property to a person i.e. trustee, is held on trust for one or more identifiable individual beneficiaries only (whether or not the
conveyance, transfer or assignment is also made to another person).

The amount remitted will be based on the difference between the ABSD (Trust)rate of 65% and ABSD rate corresponding to the profile of the beneficial owner with the highest applicable ABSD rate. ABSD
(Trust) of 65% is to be paid upfront, and an application for the refund must be made to IRAS within six months after the date of execution of the instrument.
section_path: Residential properties held on trust - ABSD (Trust)

policy_candidates.title: CPFB | Home buying guide for members below 55
policy_candidates.text:
Document: CPFB | Home buying guide for members below 55
Section: Looking to sell your current HDB flat and buy another? > Buying your next flat > **Tenancy-in-common**

**Tenancy-in-common**

If you hold the property under tenancy-in-common, you are able to sell your share in the property.

Similar to a sale of the entire property, you will be also be required to refund the principal amount of CPF used and the accrued interest (P+I) based on your respective proportions.

You might need to fork out additional cash to refund to your CPF account if you use more CPF monies than your share of property. This is to ensure that CPF members who had used more CPF savings than their share of property will still have sufficient CPF savings for their retirement and housing needs.

[Learn more](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/home-ownership/using-your-cpf-to-buy-a-home/cpf-refund-when-selling-or-transferring-property)

policy_candidates.text:
Document: Central Provident Fund (Residential Properties Scheme) Regulations 1982 - Singapore Statutes Online
Section: Section 9A Withdrawal for payment upon transfer (other than by way of sale) of residential property
Provision: 9A — Withdrawal for payment upon transfer (other than by way of sale) of residential property

Withdrawal for payment upon transfer (other than by way of sale) of residential property 9A. —(1) Where a member (called in this paragraph the transferor), being the owner or co‑owner of a residential property, will or is required to transfer (other than by way of sale) the member’s estate or interest in the residential property to another member (called in this paragraph the transferee), the transferee may apply to the Board to withdraw the whole or any part of the amount standing to the transferee’s credit in the Fund for the payment of any amount which the transferor is required, under these Regulations, to pay to the transferor’s account in the Fund upon the transfer. (2) The Board may approve an application under paragraph (1) subject to such terms and conditions as it may impose.

Find out the legal services required for your flat purchase.

The purchase of an HDB flat may require the legal services of solicitors for the transfer of the flat title and mortgage (if any).

policy_candidates.text:
Document: Terms and Conditions - Sale and Purchase of An HDB Resale Flat
Section: Terms and Conditions - Sale and Purchase of An HDB Resale Flat > **APPLICABLE TO BOTH SELLER AND BUYER**

9.6 The seller and buyer shall jointly and severally keep HDB fully indemnified against all actions, proceedings, claims, demands, liabilities, losses, charges, damages, costs and expenses which may be brought against, become payable by and/or incurred by HDB arising from or in relation to the damage caused to the flat or the building where the flat is located.

9.7 Design, Build and Sell Scheme (“DBSS”) flats are HDB flats which were designed, built and sold by private developers under Part 4B of the Housing & Development Act 1959. Any reference to a flat in these Terms and Conditions shall include a DBSS flat. Each DBSS development is characterised by its own distinctive external features. To maintain the aesthetic appearance of each development and to be in line with URA’s Gross Floor Area (GFA) Incentive Scheme, specific renovation restrictions apply to DBSS flats. These may include renovation restrictions that apply to the balcony, air-conditioner ledge, planter boxes and service yard.

The buyer must check the HDB InfoWEB (www.hdb.gov.sg) for all the renovation guidelines and restrictions that apply to DBSS flats, including but not limited to the type of renovations the buyer can or cannot do at/to the balcony, air-conditioner ledge, planter boxes, bay window and service yard, before the buyer exercises the Option to Purchase. Once the buyer has exercised the Option to Purchase, the buyer shall be deemed to have read and understood all the applicable renovation guidelines and restrictions and shall be bound by all the renovation restrictions applicable to the DBSS flat.

**24 HOUSING LOAN FROM HDB**

24.1 HDB will only grant a housing loan to the buyer who can meet the eligibility criteria. The buyer must comply with HDB’s prevailing policies, rules, regulations, terms and conditions relating to the application and approval of the HDB housing loan as stated on the HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) letter or any other loan assessment process that HDB may decide, including but not limited to the loan tenure, Loan-To-Value (LTV) limit and all other terms and conditions related to the HDB housing loan, which HDB may impose or vary from time to time.

24.2 The buyer who is eligible for and is intending to obtain a housing loan from HDB must have a valid HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) letter when he is granted an Option to Purchase by the seller. The HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) letter must be valid when the buyer submits the resale application.

24.3 The buyer who takes a housing loan from HDB must first use all his CPF savings in his Ordinary Account for the purchase of the flat up to the prevailing limits depending on the remaining lease of the flat before the loan is disbursed. HDB may allow each buyer to retain up to $20,000 in his CPF Ordinary Account or such other amount as HDB may, at its sole discretion, decide (“retention amount”). Once the buyer has endorsed the financial plan for the flat purchase, no change of the plan will be allowed.

policy_candidates.text:

Section: Housing Loan from HDB > Conditions when taking a second HDB housing loan > Additional information on cash proceeds:

HDB reserves the right to determine the amount of proceeds to be used, either by taking into account the manner of holding of the existing/last-owned HDB flat or last-owned private residential property, or according to any court order that has provided for the disposal/ division of the residential property.

Generally, flat applicants can keep the higher of $25,000 or 50% of the cash proceeds (including the cash deposit received). HDB will take into account the remaining cash proceeds when determining the second HDB housing loan amount.

[Calculate your sale proceeds](https://homes.hdb.gov.sg/home/calculator/sale-proceeds) and work out how much cash proceeds you need to use for your flat purchase. Be sure to secure sufficient financing before committing to sell your existing flat or buy another one.

supplied_policy_evidence.text:
Document: Central Provident Fund (Approved Housing Schemes) Regulations 1986 - Singapore Statutes Online
Section: Section 3A Withdrawal for payment upon transfer (other than by way of sale) of house or flat
Provision: 3A — Withdrawal for payment upon transfer (other than by way of sale) of house or flat

Withdrawal for payment upon transfer (other than by way of sale) of house or flat 3A. —(1) Where a member (called in this paragraph the transferor), being the owner or co‑owner of a house or flat, will or is required to transfer (other than by way of sale) his or her estate or interest in the house or flat to another member (called in this paragraph the transferee), the transferee may apply to the Board to withdraw the whole or any part of the amount standing to the transferee’s credit in the Fund for the payment of any amount which the transferor is required, under these Regulations, to pay to the transferor’s account in the Fund upon the transfer. (2) The Board may approve an application under paragraph (1) subject to such terms and conditions as it may deem fit to impose from time to time.

supplied_policy_evidence.title: CPFB | Home buying guide for members below 55
supplied_policy_evidence.text:
Document: CPFB | Home buying guide for members below 55
Section: Looking to sell your current HDB flat and buy another? > Buying your next flat > **Tenancy-in-common**

**Tenancy-in-common**

If you hold the property under tenancy-in-common, you are able to sell your share in the property.

Similar to a sale of the entire property, you will be also be required to refund the principal amount of CPF used and the accrued interest (P+I) based on your respective proportions.

You might need to fork out additional cash to refund to your CPF account if you use more CPF monies than your share of property. This is to ensure that CPF members who had used more CPF savings than their share of property will still have sufficient CPF savings for their retirement and housing needs.

[Learn more](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/home-ownership/using-your-cpf-to-buy-a-home/cpf-refund-when-selling-or-transferring-property)

supplied_policy_evidence.title: Terms and Conditions - Sale and Purchase of An HDB Resale Flat
supplied_policy_evidence.text:
Document: Terms and Conditions - Sale and Purchase of An HDB Resale Flat
Section: Terms and Conditions - Sale and Purchase of An HDB Resale Flat > **APPLICABLE TO THE BUYER**

Where there are two or more buyers, the buyers must indicate in the resale application form whether they wish to hold the flat as Joint-Tenants or Tenants-in-Common.

**24 HOUSING LOAN FROM HDB**

24.1 HDB will only grant a housing loan to the buyer who can meet the eligibility criteria. The buyer must comply with HDB’s prevailing policies, rules, regulations, terms and conditions relating to the application and approval of the HDB housing loan as stated on the HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) letter or any other loan assessment process that HDB may decide, including but not limited to the loan tenure, Loan-To-Value (LTV) limit and all other terms and conditions related to the HDB housing loan, which HDB may impose or vary from time to time.

24.2 The buyer who is eligible for and is intending to obtain a housing loan from HDB must have a valid HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) letter when he is granted an Option to Purchase by the seller. The HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) letter must be valid when the buyer submits the resale application.

24.3 The buyer who takes a housing loan from HDB must first use all his CPF savings in his Ordinary Account for the purchase of the flat up to the prevailing limits depending on the remaining lease of the flat before the loan is disbursed. HDB may allow each buyer to retain up to $20,000 in his CPF Ordinary Account or such other amount as HDB may, at its sole discretion, decide (“retention amount”). Once the buyer has endorsed the financial plan for the flat purchase, no change of the plan will be allowed.

policy_candidates.text:
Document: Housing Loan from HDB
Section: Housing Loan from HDB > Conditions when taking a second HDB housing loan

To promote financial prudence and prevent over-borrowing, your second HDB housing loan amount will be granted only after you have paid for the flat purchase using the full CPF refund and part of the cash proceeds received from the disposal* of the following residential properties:

Existing or last-owned HDB flat; or

Last-owned private residential property, disposed of at least 30 months, based on the legal completion date, before your HFE letter application.

* The manner of disposal includes the sale, transfer or surrender of a flat or private residential property, or by any other method under the Housing and Development Act or any other written law.

Find out the legal services required for your flat purchase.

The purchase of an HDB flat may require the legal services of solicitors for the transfer of the flat title and mortgage (if any).

policy_candidates.title: Singles
policy_candidates.text:
Document: Singles
Section: Singles > Core nucleus

A household’s eligibility for housing subsidies and HDB housing loan is assessed based on the core nucleus, which is formed by the core member(s). Core members refer to the applicant(s) and occupier(s) in an HFE letter application who enable the household to qualify for a flat purchase under an eligibility scheme. All core members must remain in the flat application, and physically reside in the flat during the [minimum occupation period (MOP)](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/buying-a-flat/bto-sbf-and-open-booking-of-flats/conditions-after-buying-a-new-flat?anchor=mop) after the flat purchase. Their names cannot be removed.

You will form a core nucleus together with the other single(s) as core applicants, and may apply for a 2-room Flexi flat from HDB or buy a resale flat on the open market.

If you are buying a flat with your sibling(s) who are orphans and single, refer to [orphaned siblings](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/buying-a-flat/flat-grant-and-loan-eligibility/couples-and-families?anchor=or-scheme).

policy_candidates.title: Housing Loan from HDB
policy_candidates.text:
Document: Housing Loan from HDB
Section: Housing Loan from HDB > What happens if I do not meet the eligibility conditions? > Use of CPF savings

Find out the requirements on the use of CPF savings for your flat purchase and for paying the monthly instalments.

Applicants have the option to:

Retain up to $20,000 of the available savings in each of their [CPF Ordinary Account (OA)](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/home-ownership/using-your-cpf-to-buy-a-home/retain-20000-in-your-oa-if-you-are-taking-a-housing-loan)

Use the savings in their CPF OA to pay the stamp fee, registration fee, legal fees, and premium for the CPF Home Protection Insurance (if applicable)

The remaining balance in your CPF OA must be used to pay for the flat purchase or take over ownership of an existing flat, before the HDB housing loan can be granted.

The total amount of CPF savings that can be used to buy or take over the flat and pay the monthly mortgage instalments will depend on:

Extent that the remaining lease of the flat can cover the youngest applicant up to the age of 95; and

Applicable CPF usage limits for the purchase of:

[New flats](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/buying-a-flat/bto-sbf-and-open-booking-of-flats/process-for-buying-a-new-flat/overview/plan-finances)

[Resale flats](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/buying-a-flat/resale-flats/process-for-buying-a-resale-flat/resale-flat-planning/mode-of-financing)

rows.question: Can I use CPF for a resale flat, and what do 4-room flats in Tampines usually sell for?
rows.answer:
Yes. You can use CPF Ordinary Account savings to buy an HDB resale flat, including for the downpayment, housing loan instalments, stamp fees and legal fees, and Home Protection Scheme premiums where applicable.[3]

Key rules and limits:
- If you take an HDB loan, each buyer may keep up to $20,000 in their OA; the remaining OA balance must be used for the flat purchase before the HDB loan can be granted.[1][4]
- CPF use is subject to limits. The amount you can use depends on whether the flat’s remaining lease can cover the youngest owner using CPF up to age 95. Once the allowed CPF amount is used up, the rest of the purchase price and/or monthly instalments must be paid in cash.[1][4][6]
- For a resale flat with an HDB loan, CPF withdrawal limits also depend on whether you can set aside the Basic Retirement Sum.[5]
- Occupiers listed in the resale application cannot use their CPF savings for the purchase.[2]
- If you later sell the flat or withdraw ownership, the CPF used plus accrued interest must be refunded to your CPF account.[2]
- For downpayment, an HDB loan’s 20% minimum can be fully paid with OA savings, while for a bank loan the 25% minimum downpayment includes 5% cash.[7]

For Tampines 4-room resale flats, in the latest 12 full months from 2025-10 to 2026-09, the median price was $665,000, the mean was $685,674, and prices ranged from $510,000 to $928,000 across 902 deals.[price]

Sources:
[1] Housing Loan from HDB: https://www.hdb.gov.sg/buying-a-flat/flat-grant-and-loan-eligibility/housing-loan/housing-loan-from-hdb
[2] Terms and Conditions - Sale and Purchase of An HDB Resale Flat: https://www.hdb.gov.sg/e-resale/resale-purchase-of-an-hdb-resale-flat
[3] CPFB | Using your CPF to buy a home: https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/home-ownership/using-your-cpf-to-buy-a-home
[4] Mode of Financing for a Resale Flat: https://www.hdb.gov.sg/buying-a-flat/resale-flats/process-for-buying-a-resale-flat/resale-flat-planning/mode-of-financing
[5] CPFB | T&C for use of CPF under CPF Housing Scheme: https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/tnc/t-c-for-use-of-cpf-under-cpf-housing-scheme
[6] Housing Loan from Financial Institutions: https://www.hdb.gov.sg/buying-a-flat/flat-grant-and-loan-eligibility/housing-loan/housing-loan-from-financial-institutions
[7] CPFB | Home buying guide for members below 55: https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/home-ownership/home-buying-guide-for-members-below-55

policy_candidates.title: Housing Loan from HDB
policy_candidates.text:
Document: Housing Loan from HDB
Section: Housing Loan from HDB > What happens if I do not meet the eligibility conditions? > Use of CPF savings

Find out the requirements on the use of CPF savings for your flat purchase and for paying the monthly instalments.

Applicants have the option to:

Retain up to $20,000 of the available savings in each of their [CPF Ordinary Account (OA)](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/home-ownership/using-your-cpf-to-buy-a-home/retain-20000-in-your-oa-if-you-are-taking-a-housing-loan)

Use the savings in their CPF OA to pay the stamp fee, registration fee, legal fees, and premium for the CPF Home Protection Insurance (if applicable)

The remaining balance in your CPF OA must be used to pay for the flat purchase or take over ownership of an existing flat, before the HDB housing loan can be granted.

The total amount of CPF savings that can be used to buy or take over the flat and pay the monthly mortgage instalments will depend on:

Extent that the remaining lease of the flat can cover the youngest applicant up to the age of 95; and

Applicable CPF usage limits for the purchase of:

[New flats](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/buying-a-flat/bto-sbf-and-open-booking-of-flats/process-for-buying-a-new-flat/overview/plan-finances)

[Resale flats](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/buying-a-flat/resale-flats/process-for-buying-a-resale-flat/resale-flat-planning/mode-of-financing)

policy_candidates.text:
Document: Terms and Conditions - Sale and Purchase of An HDB Resale Flat
Section: Terms and Conditions - Sale and Purchase of An HDB Resale Flat > **APPLICABLE TO THE BUYER**

24.5 Where the buyer obtains a housing loan from HDB, he must insure the flat against the risk of fire with HDB’s appointed insurer for a sum not less than the amount determined by HDB. HDB has the right to recall the housing loan if the buyer does not have a valid fire insurance on the flat for the duration of the housing loan.

**25 USE OF CPF SAVINGS**

The use of CPF savings for the purchase of an HDB flat is subject to the CPF Board’s prevailing policies, rules, regulations, usage limits, terms and conditions, which include but are not limited to the following:

(a) The occupiers listed in the resale application are not allowed to use their CPF savings for the purchase of the flat.

(b) The buyer who is using his CPF savings to purchase the flat will have to refund the entire sum of CPF monies used (including accrued interest) to his CPF account when he sells the flat or withdraws his ownership in the flat subsequently.

**26 HOUSING LOAN FROM FINANCIAL INSTITUTION**

26.1 The buyer may obtain a loan from any financial institution regulated by the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) to provide housing loans. The mortgage financing guidelines for housing loans obtained from financial institutions are subject to the prevailing MAS guidelines/policies/rules/directives on housing loans.

Document: CPFB | Using your CPF to buy a home
Section: Using your CPF to buy a property under the Housing Scheme > What can you use your OA savings for when buying a home?

What can you use your OA savings for when buying a home?

Your OA savings can be used to buy a HDB flat, or buy or build private and residential properties in Singapore. OA savings can also be used for downpayment and housing loan taken for the property purchase, stamp and legal fees, loan taken for the construction of your house and the purchase of vacant land (for private properties only), as well as Home Protection Scheme premiums (for HDB flats only).

policy_candidates.title: Mode of Financing for a Resale Flat
policy_candidates.text:
Document: Mode of Financing for a Resale Flat
Section: Mode of Financing for a Resale Flat > Use of CPF savings

**Retention of up to $20,000 in CPF OA**

Flat buyers taking a housing loan from HDB have the option of retaining up to $20,000 of the available [CPF savings](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/home-ownership/using-your-cpf-to-buy-a-home/retain-20000-in-your-oa-if-you-are-taking-a-housing-loan) in each buyer's OA. The remaining balance in the CPF OA must be used to pay for the flat purchase, before they can take an HDB housing loan. If you need the CPF refund from the sale of your current property to finance the resale flat purchase, please ensure the amount has already been credited to your CPF OA, before you submit the resale application.

**Conditions for use of CPF savings**

Take note of the following conditions for using your CPF savings:

There is a limit on the total amount of CPF savings that can be used for your flat purchase. Once that limit is reached, you will not be able to withdraw more of your CPF savings and have to pay the balance flat purchase price and/ or monthly mortgage instalments in cash

Section: Looking to sell your current HDB flat and buy another? > Now that you've got a flat in mind, how can you go about financing it? > Ordinary Account

Ordinary Account

Your Ordinary Account savings can be used for the downpayment and monthly instalments.

However, there are limits to the amount of Ordinary Account savings you can use for your property. Use the [Housing Usage calculator](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/tools-and-services/calculators/cpf-housing-usage) to estimate the amount.

Some expenses cannot be paid with Ordinary Account savings as well.

[Learn more](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/home-ownership/using-your-cpf-to-buy-a-home)

policy_candidates.text:
Document: CPFB | Home buying guide for members above 55
Section: Looking for your retirement home > When should you sell your flat? > If you are purchasing a resale flat

If you are purchasing a resale flat

You can take a loan to pay for the purchase. There is no need to sell the current flat first, if your loan, Ordinary Account and cash savings are enough for the purchase.

Otherwise, you may have to sell your current flat first for the sales proceeds and find interim housing arrangements. If you are thinking of using the CPF refunds for the purchase, please note that CPF refunds may take up to 15 working days to be credited to your CPF accounts.

Take note of the default [Daily Withdrawal Limit](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/article/what-type-of-cpf-withdrawals-does-the-daily-withdrawal-limit-apply-to-and-how-do-i-change-the-daily-withdrawal-limit) of $2,000 if you intend to withdraw your CPF refunds credited to your Ordinary Account.

policy_candidates.title: CPF Housing Grant for Singles Buying Resale Flats
policy_candidates.text:
Document: CPF Housing Grant for Singles Buying Resale Flats
Section: CPF Housing Grant for Singles Buying Resale Flats

If you are a first-timer Singapore Citizen (SC) and buying a resale flat on your own, you may qualify for a Singles Grant of $40,000 for the purchase of a 2- to 4- room resale flat or $25,000 for a 5-room resale flat.

If you are buying with your parents or your non-resident spouse or other first-timer single(s) (up to 2 Singles Grant applicants), you may be eligible for a Singles Grant of $40,000 for the purchase of a 2- to 4-room resale flat (i.e. a total of $80,000 for 2 singles) or $25,000 for a 5-room or bigger resale flat (i.e. a total of $50,000 for 2 singles).

In addition, you may also receive the following housing grants if you meet the respective eligibility conditions:

[Enhanced CPF Housing Grant (Singles)](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/buying-a-flat/flat-grant-and-loan-eligibility/singles/enhanced-cpf-housing-grant)

[Proximity Housing Grant (Singles)](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/buying-a-flat/flat-grant-and-loan-eligibility/singles/proximity-housing-grant)

policy_candidates.title: Mode of Financing for a Resale Flat
policy_candidates.text:
Document: Mode of Financing for a Resale Flat
Section: Mode of Financing for a Resale Flat > Use of CPF savings

**Retention of up to $20,000 in CPF OA**

Flat buyers taking a housing loan from HDB have the option of retaining up to $20,000 of the available [CPF savings](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/home-ownership/using-your-cpf-to-buy-a-home/retain-20000-in-your-oa-if-you-are-taking-a-housing-loan) in each buyer's OA. The remaining balance in the CPF OA must be used to pay for the flat purchase, before they can take an HDB housing loan. If you need the CPF refund from the sale of your current property to finance the resale flat purchase, please ensure the amount has already been credited to your CPF OA, before you submit the resale application.

**Conditions for use of CPF savings**

Take note of the following conditions for using your CPF savings:

There is a limit on the total amount of CPF savings that can be used for your flat purchase. Once that limit is reached, you will not be able to withdraw more of your CPF savings and have to pay the balance flat purchase price and/ or monthly mortgage instalments in cash

Considerations

Access to mature estates are prioritised for special groups such as first-timer families.

Mature estates are generally more expensive. For example, in previous BTO exercises, the starting selling price (excluding grants) of a 3-room flat in non-mature estates such as Choa Chu Kang was more than 30% cheaper than a 3-room flat in mature estates such as Kallang. It is important to note that the prices can fluctuate over time and may be influenced by various factors such as market conditions.

**21 ELIGIBILITY TO PURCHASE**

21.1 The buyer‘s eligibility to purchase the flat is determined with the issuance and subject to the terms and conditions of the HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) letter or any other eligibility assessment process that HDB may decide from time to time.

Any decision made by the HDB on the buyer’s eligibility to purchase the flat shall be final and conclusive.

21.3 The buyer is eligible to purchase only one flat which must be owner-occupied by the buyer and his immediate family who are authorised by HDB to stay in the flat. The buyer must be able to take physical possession of the flat on resale completion and must be in actual, exclusive and continuous occupation of the flat.

Section: Help - Resale Procedures

6.1 If there is a recess area space fronting the flat available for sale, the buyers may request HDB to process the application to buy the recess area together with the resale application. The buyers must [write to us](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/write-to-us) to request information on the availability of the recess area for purchase at least 2 weeks before submitting the resale application. As the resale completion date may be affected/delayed, the seller’s consent will need to be obtained before HDB can process the 2 applications concurrently. In the absence of the seller’s consent, HDB will process the resale application without the purchase of the recess area.

**7 RESALE APPLICATION**

7.1 The sellers and buyers have to submit their respective portion of the resale application separately to HDB with attachment of the required documents via the HDB Flat Portal. Their salesperson (if any) can submit the application on their behalf via the e-Resale System or Estate Agent Toolkit.

7.2 The sellers and buyers will each have to pay an administrative fee (inclusive of GST) of $40 (1/2-room flats) or $80 (3-room and bigger flats). The payment will be via the payment modes provided in the HDB Flat Portal/e-Resale System/Estate Agent Toolkit.

7.3 Either the sellers or the buyers may submit their portion of the resale application first. The second party will have to do so within 7 days. If not, the submission by the first party will lapse and they have to re-start the process. The administrative fee paid is non-refundable.
